blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the logs through the error message) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail when the purpose needs the name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep personal data out of the error message: throw `new NotFoundError("no customer")` (or any constant text). `errorHandler` in `src/server.ts` logs `err.message` (`logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`), and `src/logger.ts` ships every line to the log platform, so each lookup of an unknown address by a support agent stores that typed e-mail address — of a customer or of anyone — in the logs with no retention rule (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 5(1)(e), 32). The same applies, with less impact, to `no customer ${id}` at `src/support.ts:32`, which logs the customer identifier: drop it too.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the logs through the error message

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — the proposal says the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to": `id` (opaque) and `name`. Remove `email`, `phone`, `birthDate` and `address`; the agent can look the rest up internally by id. As written, every signed-in customer who opens a page with the chat has their full record shared with a third-party processor and returned to the browser by `GET /chat/settings` (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 28). Load only the needed columns in `customerById` for this route.
findings.title: Chat vendor Helply receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail when the purpose needs the name

findings.evidence: /** What the Helply chat widget is started with, for the signed-in customer. */
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: is Helply covered by a processor agreement (GDPR Art. 28), recorded in the records of processing (Art. 30), and where does it store data — a transfer outside the EEA needs Chapter V safeguards? State the lawful basis of sharing chat identity with it, and how erasure and access requests reach the copies Helply keeps. Only the controller can answer; nothing in the change or the repository says.
findings.title: Helply is a new processor with no stated legal basis, contract or transfer location

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The proposal's purpose is that agents stop asking customers who they are; it does not say agents need the birth date, postal address or phone of every customer they look up. Return only the fields the support console shows (likely `id`, `name`, `email`), or state in the proposal why each further field is needed (e.g. identity checks) — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c). Whether the console uses them could not be verified from the repository.
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date, address and phone without a stated need
